You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

memory_entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC periodic stripe tiling from sparse stripe clues", content="For ARC tasks where the input contains sparse full-width horizontal stripes or diagonal stripes and the output expands them into a full periodic tiling: identify each distinct nonzero stripe as a clue, determine its stripe-coordinate (horizontal rows: row index; down-right diagonal: k=column-row), and use the number of distinct clue stripes as the period. Each clue fixes the color at its coordinate modulo that period; repeat those colors cyclically across the whole grid, filling every cell (no zeros). For horizontal rows, output is constant across each row. For down-right diagonals, output is constant on c-r diagonals, i.e. output[r][c]=motif[(c-r) mod period]. Example from task-03e48a56: clues are color 5 on c-r=-5 and color 6 on c-r=-10, so two stripes imply period 2; even k gets 6 and odd k gets 5, producing a checkerboard. Examples showed row-stripe clue counts 4, 6, and 8 yielding periods 4, 6, and 8, and a five-diagonal motif yielding period 5. The motif may include duplicate adjacent colors; preserve clue phase from actual coordinates.", path="arc", global_=True, metadata={"task_type":"periodic_stripe_tiling","confidence":"demonstrated"})
print(memory_entry)
